title: New York Board of Regents enforcement-action summaries for Helen M. Fogarty (a/k/a Helen Moses) and Marc Rice
authors: New York State Education Department Office of the Professions; New York State Board of Regents
publication: New York State Office of the Professions Enforcement Actions
access_status: official regulator HTML inspected for the June 12 and July 18, 1997 psychology dispositions and for the regulator's description of authority
evidence_scope: Two final professional-discipline summaries involving psychologists linked to the Sullivanian lead by F-156; the official pages themselves do not name the Sullivan Institute
sequence_allegation: professional-misconduct charges involving therapist-patient or supervisor relationships, billing, undue influence, family contact, and sexual conduct
sequence_assessment: Office of the Professions investigation and prosecution followed by Board of Regents final disposition; the public summaries do not expose the complete evidentiary record
sequence_intervention: license revocation and a $15,000 fine for Fogarty/Moses; license revocation for Rice
sequence_review: Board of Regents final disposition; underlying charges, findings, hearing records, and any appellate record were not available on the summary pages
sequence_later_outcome: professional authority was removed; no child, family, patient-recovery, institutional-remedy, or later safeguarding outcome is reported
notes: Fogarty/Moses: Psychology license 003729, calendar 01281, June 12, 1997. Rice: Psychology license 003903, calendar 10401, July 18, 1997; companion official page https://www.op.nysed.gov/enforcement/enforcement-actions?page=854. The official record corroborates two dispositions, not every person or causal link reported in F-156

title: Whanaketia: final inquiry findings and Recommendation 88 concerning Gloriavale
authors: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Historical Abuse in State Care and in the Care of Faith-based Institutions
publication: Whanaketia — Through pain and trauma, from darkness to light
access_status: official Royal Commission final-report HTML, findings, institutional-response material, government-briefing summary, and recommendations inspected
evidence_scope: Final inquiry record combining survivor evidence, an institutional-response hearing, policy material, criminal-history records, and government briefings; historical scope is principally 1950-1999 with later correction context through December 2023
sequence_allegation: survivor reports of physical, sexual, spiritual, economic, educational, and medical abuse or neglect and blocked external reporting
sequence_assessment: Royal Commission evidence process using testimony, witness statements, institutional hearing evidence, policies, official records, and disclosed government briefings
sequence_intervention: external police and child-protection responses; a cross-agency government coordinating function from August 2022 through December 2023; safety-plan context; Gloriavale-specific Recommendation 88
sequence_review: final inquiry findings, oversight recommendations, and a direction that ongoing safety remain a government responsibility rather than an internal assurance
sequence_later_outcome: the coordination function ended while official briefings still recorded child-wellbeing risks; Recommendation 88 is a correction requirement, not proof that implementation or later safety was achieved
notes: Companion official sections include https://www.abuseincare.org.nz/reports/whanaketia/part-7/chapter-5, https://www.abuseincare.org.nz/reports/whanaketia/part-7/chapter-8, https://www.abuseincare.org.nz/reports/whanaketia/part-4/chapter-4-6, and https://www.abuseincare.org.nz/reports/whanaketia/preliminaries/recommendations. Any charge status quoted by the report is historical as of its cited briefing and was not promoted as current in 2026

lane: adjacent statutory inquiry and external reporting
title: Child protection in religious organisations and settings investigation report
authors: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse Inquiry Panel
publication: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse
access_status: complete official statutory-inquiry web report, Jesus Fellowship section, conclusions, recommendations, cited hearing transcript, and police evidence references inspected
evidence_scope: Thematic statutory-inquiry record; Jesus Fellowship evidence connects survivor testimony about communal disclosure barriers with police-supplied Operation Lifeboat prosecution counts and sector-wide conclusions
sequence_allegation: survivor testimony described child abuse, disbelief, blame, prayer or relocation responses, distrust of outside bodies, reputation pressure, and forgiveness used after disclosure
sequence_assessment: public-hearing testimony and documentary evidence, including Northamptonshire Police materials; the report distinguishes allegations, prosecutions, and convictions
sequence_intervention: 2013 public invitation for disclosures; transfer to police; Operation Lifeboat investigation; trials and convictions; inquiry recommendations for policies, professional advice, victim-focused procedures, training, and wider oversight
sequence_review: statutory inquiry analysis; the report states internal discipline is not a substitute for external reporting, justice, redress, or risk assessment
sequence_later_outcome: the report recorded six convicted perpetrators for offences relating to 11 children and a then-ongoing further investigation; it did not supply later survivor wellbeing, complete prevalence, redress, or post-report implementation outcomes
notes: Published September 2, 2021. Companion official pages include the Jesus Fellowship evidence section, conclusions, recommendations, records section, and hearing transcript. The inquiry reproduced some witness characterizations that are not adopted here as diagnoses or danger proxies
